meta.title: Botworks — Put AI to work on the business you actually run
meta.description: Botworks is an AI transformation partner for executives who want to turn an important operational problem into something useful, reliable, and owned by the company.

hero.heading: Put AI to work on the business you actually run.
hero.body: You have a hunch that important work could be done better with AI. Botworks investigates the problem, builds the right answer, and stays responsible until people can rely on it.
hero.note: The work creates value now. The code, rules, data, and decisions stay legible enough for employees and AI agents to keep improving it.

proof.heading: Three companies. Three different answers.
proof.body: The point is not to force every problem into an AI agent or a custom application. The point is to make consequential work better, then make the result hold up in daily use.

items.heading: One site visit now feeds operations, client reporting, and estimating.
items.body: Account managers capture notes and photos in the field, including on weak cell service. The same record supports supervisor review, crew follow-up, client PDFs, and a measured estimating system.
items.detail: The difficult part was not generating an app. It was weeks of testing uploads, failure states, real field behavior, and the pricing rules the company actually uses.

items.heading: Reporting that can be rerun, reconciled, and challenged.
items.body: Route, billing, payroll, card-sheet, and operating data now feed a repeatable executive snapshot and owner-operator transaction work instead of a one-off spreadsheet exercise.
items.detail: The work includes definitions, source mapping, reconciliation, tests, and the discipline to present the math without pretending to know what it means for the operator.

items.heading: A job number becomes a rebate packet without re-keying the same facts.
items.body: The system reads the company’s existing job data, applies the local program rules, lets the operator review the result, and produces the paperwork the office needs.
items.detail: A narrow custom workflow made sense because the useful data already existed and the remaining work lived inside a program-specific portal and form process.

premise.heading: Access to AI is not the hard part.
paragraphs: Most executives I meet already use ChatGPT, Claude, or another AI tool. Their teams are capable too. The gap is finding the time and ownership to investigate a problem, work through the data, build something, test real cases, deploy it, and keep it working.

That is where Botworks fits. A good engagement starts with an honest conversation and access to the relevant people, data, or systems. It should become tangible quickly: software, an analysis, a reporting surface, a processing tool, or a clear decision not to build.

work.heading: The role changes with the problem.
work.body: On one engagement I may be doing product work, engineering, data analysis, operational investigation, or all four. The buyer should not have to diagnose which technical job title is missing before asking for help.

items.heading: Find the real problem
items.body: Read the files, map the workflow, inspect the data, and separate a fixable annoyance from work that is important enough to change.

items.heading: Make something useful
items.body: Move quickly from discussion to a concrete output people can see, test, and use. The first useful thing is often the fastest way to learn what the company actually needs.

items.heading: Take production seriously
items.body: If people log in or depend on the answer, permissions, monitoring, exceptions, data integrity, documentation, and maintenance are part of the work.

judgment.eyebrow: Build only when the work warrants it
judgment.heading: Good software already exists. Botworks is not here to replace it for sport.
judgment.body: If a SaaS product, a configuration change, or a small automation solves the material problem, that is usually the right answer. Custom software creates an ongoing responsibility for security, support, integrations, and maintenance. It is worth building when the workflow is specific, consequential, poorly served by the market, and valuable enough to own.
judgment.principle: Use the good product. Connect what should be connected. Build the part that is genuinely yours.

buyer.heading: The common trait is authority, not title.
buyer.body: Botworks works best with an owner, CEO, CFO, COO, CMO, senior operator, or private-equity operating partner who can provide access, make decisions, and get the work moving.
buyer.fit: A good prospect has an operational itch: something is slower, more manual, less visible, or less reliable than it should be—and they suspect AI could help but do not have someone carrying it into production.
buyer.notFit: This is a poor fit when an existing tool already solves the important part, the work cannot reach the relevant data or people, or every decision must pass through months of approval before anyone can test it.

ownership.heading: The client should be able to continue the work without Botworks.
ownership.body: Engagements commonly run as a monthly retainer. That is payment for ongoing work—not a claim on the client’s future. Client-specific systems are designed for a clean transition if the relationship ends.

Operational data, definitions, rules, and tests
Documentation for employees, future maintainers, and AI agents

about.heading: Hi, I’m Matt.
paragraphs: I spent 15 years in software product management, most recently as a VP of Product Management. I was used to having engineers, designers, analysts, and product people around the table. Most operating companies do not—and it would be a strange use of their budget to recreate that whole department.

Botworks is a practical version of that capability: one accountable partner, AI agents doing a great deal of the production work, and specialists brought in when the problem genuinely needs them. I care about getting to the truth, shipping something people can use, and leaving the work understandable when I am gone.

bottomCta.heading: What is the problem you keep thinking AI should be able to help with?
bottomCta.body: Send me the rough version. You do not need a specification, a budget category, or the right technical language.
